title: Κλέπται καὶ ἀλεκτρυών
part: The Thieves and the Cock (Chambry 158 · Perry 122)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 158 (= Perry 122). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Κλέπται εἴς τινα οἰκίαν εἰσελθόντες οὐδὲν μὲν ἄλλο εὗρον, μόνον δὲ ἀλεκτρυόνα, καὶ τοῦτον λαβόντες ἀπηλλάγησαν.
sentences.tr: Kleptai eis tina oikian eiselthontes ouden men allo heuron, monon de alektryona, kai touton labontes apēllagēsan.
sentences.l: Thieves, having gone into a certain house, found nothing else, but only a cock, and having taken him they went off.
sentences.i: Some thieves got into a house and found nothing there but a cock; so they took him and made off.
sentences.n: μέν … δέ sets "nothing else" against "only a cock" — the pairing marks the contrast and is not translated by any one English word. ἀπηλλάγησαν is aorist passive in form but middle in sense, "they took themselves off".

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ μέλλων ὑπ’ αὐτῶν θύεσθαι ἐδέετο ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολύσωσι, λέγων χρήσιμον ἑαυτὸν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις εἶναι νύκτωρ αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τὰ ἔργα ἐγείροντα.
sentences.tr: Ho de mellōn hyp’ autōn thyesthai edeeto hopōs auton apolysōsi, legōn chrēsimon heauton tois anthrōpois einai nyktōr autous epi ta erga egeironta.
sentences.l: And he, being about to be sacrificed by them, begged that they let him go, saying that he was useful to men, rousing them by night to their work.
sentences.i: And when he was on the point of being sacrificed, he begged them to let him go, saying that he was of use to men, since he woke them by night for their work.
sentences.n: θύω is properly "sacrifice"; in ordinary use it also covers killing a beast for the table, and both senses are alive here. δέομαι with ὅπως and the aorist subjunctive is the regular construction of a request. λέγων introduces accusative and infinitive, and ἐγείροντα agrees with ἑαυτόν inside it, giving the ground of χρήσιμον.

sentences.t: Οἱ δὲ ὑποτυχόντες ἔφασαν· « Ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τοῦτό σε μᾶλλον θύομεν· ἐκείνους γὰρ ἐγείρων ἡμᾶς οὐκ ἐᾷς κλέπτειν. »
sentences.tr: Hoi de hypotychontes ephasan· « Alla kai dia touto se mallon thyomen· ekeinous gar egeirōn hēmas ouk eāis kleptein. »
sentences.l: But they, taking-up-the-word, said: « But for this very reason we sacrifice you the more; for by rousing those men you do not let us steal. »
sentences.i: But they took up the word and said: « That is the very reason we are the readier to kill you; for by waking them you leave us no chance to steal. »
sentences.n: ὑποτυχόντες is "taking up the word, answering" — nothing to do with laying hold of anything. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο, "for this very reason", turns the cock's own plea back on him. ἐάω takes the infinitive of what is allowed.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι ταῦτα μάλιστα τοῖς πονηροῖς ἠναντίωται ἅτινα τῶν χρηστῶν ἐστιν εὐεργετήματα.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti tauta malista tois ponērois ēnantiōtai hatina tōn chrēstōn estin euergetēmata.
sentences.l: The story shows that those things are most opposed to the wicked which are benefits to the honest.
sentences.i: The story shows that the very things which are benefits to honest men are what stand most in the way of the wicked.
sentences.n: ἠναντίωται is the perfect of ἐναντιόομαι with the dative of the party opposed; the perfect states a standing state of affairs, not a past act. ἅτινα is the indefinite relative, "whatever things". τῶν χρηστῶν is possessive: the benefits that belong to honest men.
